LESSON: GRAMMAR IN USE 11.3.1 LANGUAGE PATTERNS

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 11
Topic 11.3: Grammar in Use 11.3.1 Language Patterns

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Grammar in Use 11.3.1 Language Patterns. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify interrogatives in a variety of texts for communication clarity
2. use interrogatives in a variety of contexts for effective communication
3. respond to a variety of questions based on interrogatives for effective communication

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE LEARNING: GRAMMAR IN USE 11.3.1 LANGUAGE PATTERNS
Grammar in Use 11.3.1 Language Patterns is a Grade mathematics skill used at school, at the market, and at home.

HOW TO STUDY THIS TOPIC
1. Read each idea slowly.
2. Copy every worked example into your book and recalculate it yourself.
3. Then try the practice questions without looking at the answers.

WORKED EXAMPLE STYLE
Write the question clearly. Show each step. Box the final answer.
Example framework:
  Question: (write a Grammar in Use 11.3.1 Language Patterns problem)
  Step 1: …
  Step 2: …
  Answer: …

KENYAN CONTEXT
Use shillings, market goods, school desks, or garden plots as story numbers so the maths feels real.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Solve one simple Grammar in Use 11.3.1 Language Patterns question using objects or a drawing.

Example 2: Solve a harder Grammar in Use 11.3.1 Language Patterns question showing every step.

Example 3: Make a word problem about Grammar in Use 11.3.1 Language Patterns set at a Kenyan market.

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write and solve five questions on Grammar in Use 11.3.1 Language Patterns.
2. Explain one solution aloud to a parent or friend.
3. Invent one new word problem and solve it.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. Complete 10 practice questions on Grammar in Use 11.3.1 Language Patterns in your exercise book.
2. Mark your work. Redo any question you missed.
3. Teach a younger learner one method from this lesson.

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. identify interrogatives in a variety of texts for communication clarity
2. use interrogatives in a variety of contexts for effective communication
3. respond to a variety of questions based on interrogatives for effective communication

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.
